question: How long do created marshes take to reach biodiversity and function comparable to natural reference wetlands, and which attributes lag?
text: The included studies do not tell us how long a created marsh takes to match a natural wetland. The comparisons below describe conditions at particular ages, not a full recovery timeline. Growth, size and the amount of living material were lower in created and restored marshes than in natural wetlands, with high certainty. Two of the three studies found fewer species, with moderate certainty. Plant cover and survival were also lower. Each finding came from one study, with very low certainty for plant cover and low certainty for survival. One study each found higher numbers of plants and other organisms, more reproduction, mixed results for animal numbers, and an unclear difference in which species were present and how common they were. All four findings had very low certainty. As marshes aged, studies found no clear change in which species were present and how common they were, with moderate certainty. They also found no clear change in the number of species or in how many invasive organisms were present, with very low certainty. No matching comparisons with natural wetlands were found for how ecosystems function, water flow or landforms, soil conditions, soil and water chemistry, pollutants, new plants becoming established, animal behaviour or invasive species.
